sanskrit: kālopahatacitto hi sarvo muhyati bhārata yathā mūḍho bhavān pūrvam asminn arthe samudyate
english: For every man whose mind is overthrown by Time grows bewildered, O Bhārata, even as you yourself, deluded before, rose up in this very matter.

sanskrit: kim anyat kālayogād dhi diṣṭam eva parāyaṇam mā ca doṣaṃ mahārāja pāṇḍaveṣu niveśaya
english: What else is there but the working of Time? Destiny alone is the final refuge. Lay not the blame, O great king, upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: alpo 'py atikramo nāsti pāṇḍavānāṃ mahātmanām dharmato nyāyataś caiva snehataś ca paraṃtapa
english: Not the slightest transgression is there in the great-souled Pāṇḍavas, neither in righteousness, nor in justice, nor in affection, O scorcher of foes.

sanskrit: etat sarvaṃ tu vijñāya ātmadoṣakṛtaṃ phalam asūyāṃ pāṇḍuputreṣu na bhavān kartum arhati
english: Knowing all this to be the fruit wrought by your own fault, you ought not to harbor resentment against the sons of Pāṇḍu.

sanskrit: kulaṃ vaṃśaś ca piṇḍaś ca yac ca putrakṛtaṃ phalam gāndhāryās tava caivādya pāṇḍaveṣu pratiṣṭhitam
english: Your lineage, your line of descent, the funeral offering, and the fruit that a son procures — for both you and Gāndhārī all of these now rest upon the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: etat sarvam anudhyātvā ātmanaś ca vyatikramam śivena pāṇḍavān dhyāhi namas te bharatarṣabha
english: Reflecting upon all this, and upon your own offense, turn your thoughts toward the Pāṇḍavas with goodwill. Homage to you, O bull of the Bharatas.

sanskrit: jānāsi ca mahābāho dharmarājasya yā tvayi bhaktir bharataśārdūla snehaś cāpi svabhāvataḥ
english: You know full well, O mighty-armed one, O tiger of the Bharatas, what devotion the Dharmarāja bears toward you, and what natural affection too.

sanskrit: etac ca kadanaṃ kṛtvā śatrūṇām apakāriṇām dahyate sma divārātraṃ na ca śarmādhigacchati
english: Even having wrought this slaughter of the offending foe, he burns with grief day and night, and finds no peace at all.

sanskrit: tvāṃ caiva naraśārdūla gāndhārīṃ ca yaśasvinīm sa śocan bharataśreṣṭha na śāntim adhigacchati
english: Grieving for you, O tiger among men, and for the renowned Gāndhārī, O best of the Bharatas, he finds no calm.

sanskrit: hriyā ca parayāviṣṭo bhavantaṃ nādhigacchati putraśokābhisaṃtaptaṃ buddhivyākulitendriyam
english: Overcome by the deepest shame, he dares not approach you — you who are consumed by sorrow for your sons, your senses confounded in mind.

sanskrit: evam uktvā mahārāja dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ yadūttamaḥ uvāca paramaṃ vākyaṃ gāndhārīṃ śokakarśitām
english: Having spoken thus to Dhṛtarāṣṭra, O great king, the foremost of the Yadus addressed these supreme words to Gāndhārī, wasted with grief.

sanskrit: saubaleyi nibodha tvaṃ yat tvāṃ vakṣyāmi suvrate tvatsamā nāsti loke 'sminn adya sīmantinī śubhe
english: O daughter of Subala, hear what I shall say to you, O woman of noble vows. There is no woman equal to you this day in all this world, O auspicious one.

sanskrit: jānāmi ca yathā rājñi sabhāyāṃ mama saṃnidhau dharmārthasahitaṃ vākyam ubhayoḥ pakṣayor hitam uktavaty asi kalyāṇi na ca te tanayaiḥ śrutam
english: I know, O queen, how in the assembly, in my presence, you spoke a word fraught with righteousness and gain, beneficial to both parties, O gracious lady — yet it was not heeded by your sons.

sanskrit: duryodhanas tvayā cokto jayārthī paruṣaṃ vacaḥ śṛṇu mūḍha vaco mahyaṃ yato dharmas tato jayaḥ
english: To Duryodhana, hungry for victory, you spoke a stern word: 'Hear my word, O fool — where righteousness is, there is victory.'

sanskrit: tad idaṃ samanuprāptaṃ tava vākyaṃ nṛpātmaje evaṃ viditvā kalyāṇi mā sma śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ vināśāya mā te buddhiḥ kadā cana
english: That word of yours, O daughter of a king, has now come wholly true. Knowing this, O gracious one, set not your mind upon grief, and let your thought never turn to the destruction of the Pāṇḍavas.

sanskrit: śaktā cāsi mahābhāge pṛthivīṃ sacarācarām cakṣuṣā krodhadīptena nirdagdhuṃ tapaso balāt
english: For you are able, O greatly blessed one, by the power of your austerities, to burn up the earth with all that moves and is unmoving, with an eye kindled by wrath.

sanskrit: vāsudevavacaḥ śrutvā gāndhārī vākyam abravīt evam etan mahābāho yathā vadasi keśava
english: Hearing the words of Vāsudeva, Gāndhārī spoke: 'It is even so, O mighty-armed one, as you say, O Keśava.'

sanskrit: ādhibhir dahyamānāyā matiḥ saṃcalitā mama sā me vyavasthitā śrutvā tava vākyaṃ janārdana
english: My mind, scorched by anguish, had been set trembling; but now, hearing your word, O Janārdana, it has grown steadfast.

sanskrit: rājñas tv andhasya vṛddhasya hataputrasya keśava tvaṃ gatiḥ saha tair vīraiḥ pāṇḍavair dvipadāṃ vara
english: For this old, blind king, bereft of his sons, O Keśava, you are now the refuge, together with those heroes, the Pāṇḍavas, O best of men.

sanskrit: etāvad uktvā vacanaṃ mukhaṃ pracchādya vāsasā putraśokābhisaṃtaptā gāndhārī praruroda ha
english: Having spoken only this much, covering her face with her garment, Gāndhārī, consumed with sorrow for her sons, broke into loud weeping.

sanskrit: tata enāṃ mahābāhuḥ keśavaḥ śokakarśitām hetukāraṇasaṃyuktair vākyair āśvāsayat prabhuḥ
english: Then the mighty-armed lord Keśava consoled her, wasted with grief, with words fraught with reason and argument.

sanskrit: samāśvāsya ca gāndhārīṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca mādhavaḥ drauṇeḥ saṃkalpitaṃ bhāvam anvabudhyata keśavaḥ
english: And having comforted Gāndhārī and Dhṛtarāṣṭra, Mādhava, Keśava, perceived the resolve that the son of Droṇa had conceived.

sanskrit: tatas tvarita utthāya pādau mūrdhnā praṇamya ca dvaipāyanasya rājendra tataḥ kauravam abravīt
english: Then, rising in haste and bowing his head to the feet of Dvaipāyana, O lord of kings, he spoke thus to the Kaurava:

sanskrit: āpṛcche tvāṃ kuruśreṣṭha mā ca śoke manaḥ kṛthāḥ drauṇeḥ pāpo 'sty abhiprāyas tenāsmi sahasotthitaḥ pāṇḍavānāṃ vadhe rātrau buddhis tena pradarśitā
english: 'I take my leave of you, O best of the Kurus; do not set your mind on grief. The son of Droṇa harbors an evil purpose, and for that reason have I risen up in haste; this night his mind has shown itself bent on the slaughter of the Pāṇḍavas.'

sanskrit: etac chrutvā tu vacanaṃ gāndhāryā sahito 'bravīt dhṛtarāṣṭro mahābāhuḥ keśavaṃ keśisūdanam
english: Hearing this word, the mighty-armed Dhṛtarāṣṭra, together with Gāndhārī, spoke to Keśava, the slayer of Keśin:

sanskrit: śīghraṃ gaccha mahābāho pāṇḍavān paripālaya bhūyas tvayā sameṣyāmi kṣipram eva janārdana prāyāt tatas tu tvarito dārukeṇa sahācyutaḥ
english: 'Go swiftly, O mighty-armed one, and guard the Pāṇḍavas; I shall meet with you again right soon, O Janārdana.' Then Acyuta set forth in haste, together with Dāruka.

sanskrit: vāsudeve gate rājan dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ janeśvaram āśvāsayad ameyātmā vyāso lokanamaskṛtaḥ
english: When Vāsudeva had departed, O king, Vyāsa of measureless soul, revered by all the worlds, consoled Dhṛtarāṣṭra, the lord of men.

sanskrit: vāsudevo 'pi dharmātmā kṛtakṛtyo jagāma ha śibiraṃ hāstinapurād didṛkṣuḥ pāṇḍavān nṛpa
english: And Vāsudeva too, the righteous-souled, his purpose accomplished, set out from Hāstinapura toward the camp, desiring to behold the Pāṇḍavas, O king.

sanskrit: āgamya śibiraṃ rātrau so 'bhyagacchata pāṇḍavān tac ca tebhyaḥ samākhyāya sahitas taiḥ samāviśat
english: Reaching the camp by night, he came to the Pāṇḍavas, and having reported all to them, he settled down in their company.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca adhiṣṭhitaḥ padā mūrdhni bhagnasaktho mahīṃ gataḥ śauṭīramānī putro me kāny abhāṣata saṃjaya
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: My son, his thighs shattered, fallen to the earth, his head trodden under foot, proud of his might — what words did he utter, O Saṃjaya?

sanskrit: atyarthaṃ kopano rājā jātavairaś ca pāṇḍuṣu vyasanaṃ paramaṃ prāptaḥ kim āha paramāhave
english: That king, exceedingly prone to wrath and bearing inveterate enmity against the sons of Pāṇḍu, having met with utter ruin in that supreme combat — what did he say?

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca śṛṇu rājan pravakṣyāmi yathāvṛttaṃ narādhipa rājñā yad uktaṃ bhagnena tasmin vyasana āgate
english: Saṃjaya said: Hear, O king; I shall relate it as it befell, O ruler of men — what was spoken by the broken king when that calamity had come upon him.

sanskrit: bhagnasaktho nṛpo rājan pāṃsunā so 'vaguṇṭhitaḥ yamayan mūrdhajāṃs tatra vīkṣya caiva diśo daśa
english: With his thighs shattered, the king, O monarch, was covered over with dust; gathering up his hair, and gazing about at the ten directions,

sanskrit: keśān niyamya yatnena niḥśvasann urago yathā saṃrambhāśruparītābhyāṃ netrābhyām abhivīkṣya mām
english: binding up his hair with effort, hissing like a serpent, with eyes brimming with tears of fury he looked upon me,

sanskrit: bāhū dharaṇyāṃ niṣpiṣya muhur matta iva dvipaḥ prakīrṇān mūrdhajān dhunvan dantair dantān upaspṛśan garhayan pāṇḍavaṃ jyeṣṭhaṃ niḥśvasyedam athābravīt
english: and pounding his arms upon the ground again and again, like an elephant in rut, shaking his scattered locks, grinding tooth against tooth, reviling the eldest of the Pāṇḍavas, he sighed and then spoke thus:

sanskrit: bhīṣme śāṃtanave nāthe karṇe cāstrabhṛtāṃ vare gautame śakunau cāpi droṇe cāstrabhṛtāṃ vare
english: 'With Bhīṣma, son of Śaṃtanu, as my protector, with Karṇa, foremost of those who bear arms, with Gautama and Śakuni too, and with Droṇa, foremost of those who bear arms —

sanskrit: aśvatthāmni tathā śalye śūre ca kṛtavarmaṇi imām avasthāṃ prāpto 'smi kālo hi duratikramaḥ
english: with Aśvatthāman likewise, and Śalya, and the valiant Kṛtavarman — yet to this state have I come; for Time is hard indeed to overpass.'

sanskrit: ekādaśacamūbhartā so 'ham etāṃ daśāṃ gataḥ kālaṃ prāpya mahābāho na kaś cid ativartate
english: 'I, the lord of eleven armies, have come to this plight! When Time comes upon him, O mighty-armed one, no one prevails against it.'

sanskrit: ākhyātavyaṃ madīyānāṃ ye 'smiñ jīvanti saṃgare yathāhaṃ bhīmasenena vyutkramya samayaṃ hataḥ
english: 'It must be told to those of my own who yet live in this battle — how I was slain by Bhīmasena in violation of the rules of fair fight.'

sanskrit: bahūni sunṛśaṃsāni kṛtāni khalu pāṇḍavaiḥ bhūriśravasi karṇe ca bhīṣme droṇe ca śrīmati
english: 'Many most cruel deeds have indeed been done by the Pāṇḍavas — against Bhūriśravas, against Karṇa, against Bhīṣma, and against the illustrious Droṇa.'

sanskrit: idaṃ cākīrtijaṃ karma nṛśaṃsaiḥ pāṇḍavaiḥ kṛtam yena te satsu nirvedaṃ gamiṣyantīti me matiḥ
english: 'And this infamous deed too has been wrought by the cruel Pāṇḍavas, whereby, among the good, they shall come to be despised — such is my conviction.'

sanskrit: kā prītiḥ sattvayuktasya kṛtvopadhikṛtaṃ jayam ko vā samayabhettāraṃ budhaḥ saṃmantum arhati
english: 'What joy can there be for a man of true worth in a victory won by trickery? And what wise man would deign to commend the breaker of compacts?'

sanskrit: adharmeṇa jayaṃ labdhvā ko nu hṛṣyeta paṇḍitaḥ yathā saṃhṛṣyate pāpaḥ pāṇḍuputro vṛkodaraḥ
english: 'What learned man would rejoice at a victory gained by unrighteousness, as that wicked son of Pāṇḍu, Vṛkodara, rejoices?'

sanskrit: kiṃ nu citram atas tv adya bhagnasakthasya yan mama kruddhena bhīmasenena pādena mṛditaṃ śiraḥ
english: 'And what wonder is there in this — that today, my thighs being broken, my head was crushed with his foot by the enraged Bhīmasena?'

sanskrit: pratapantaṃ śriyā juṣṭaṃ vartamānaṃ ca bandhuṣu evaṃ kuryān naro yo hi sa vai saṃjaya pūjitaḥ
english: 'Against one resplendent, blessed with fortune, and moving honorably among his kin — the man who would act thus, O Saṃjaya, is he then to be esteemed?'

sanskrit: abhijñau kṣatradharmasya mama mātā pitā ca me tau hi saṃjaya duḥkhārtau vijñāpyau vacanān mama
english: 'My mother and my father both know well the duty of the warrior caste; those two, O Saṃjaya, stricken with grief, are to be informed in my words.'

sanskrit: iṣṭaṃ bhṛtyā bhṛtāḥ samyag bhūḥ praśāstā sasāgarā mūrdhni sthitam amitrāṇāṃ jīvatām eva saṃjaya
english: 'Sacrifices have I performed, my servants well maintained, the sea-girt earth duly ruled; while my foes yet lived, I stood upon their heads, O Saṃjaya.'

sanskrit: dattā dāyā yathāśakti mitrāṇāṃ ca priyaṃ kṛtam amitrā bādhitāḥ sarve ko nu svantataro mayā
english: 'Gifts have I bestowed according to my power, and kindness done to friends; all my enemies have been crushed — who then has come to a better end than I?'

sanskrit: yātāni pararāṣṭrāṇi nṛpā bhuktāś ca dāsavat priyebhyaḥ prakṛtaṃ sādhu ko nu svantataro mayā
english: 'The realms of others have I overrun, and kings I have made to serve me like slaves; good have I done to those dear to me — who then has come to a better end than I?'

sanskrit: mānitā bāndhavāḥ sarve mānyaḥ saṃpūjito janaḥ tritayaṃ sevitaṃ sarvaṃ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: 'All my kinsmen have I honored, every worthy person duly revered; the threefold ends of life have all been pursued — who then has come to a better end than I?'

sanskrit: ājñaptaṃ nṛpamukhyeṣu mānaḥ prāptaḥ sudurlabhaḥ ājāneyais tathā yātaṃ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: 'My command has held sway over the chief among kings, and honor most hard to win was mine; borne I was by steeds of noble breed — who then has come to a better end than I?'

sanskrit: adhītaṃ vidhivad dattaṃ prāptam āyur nirāmayam svadharmeṇa jitā lokāḥ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: 'The Veda I have studied, gifts duly bestowed, a span of life free from disease attained; by my own duty I have won the higher worlds — who then has come to a better end than I?'

sanskrit: diṣṭyā nāhaṃ jitaḥ saṃkhye parān preṣyavad āśritaḥ diṣṭyā me vipulā lakṣmīr mṛte tv anyaṃ gatā vibho
english: 'By good fortune I was not vanquished in battle so as to depend upon foes like a menial; by good fortune my ample royal splendor has passed, at my death, to another, O lord.'

sanskrit: yad iṣṭaṃ kṣatrabandhūnāṃ svadharmam anutiṣṭhatām nidhanaṃ tan mayā prāptaṃ ko nu svantataro mayā
english: 'That death which is the desire of warriors who hold fast to their own duty — that very death I have attained; who then has come to a better end than I?'

sanskrit: diṣṭyā nāhaṃ parāvṛtto vairāt prākṛtavaj jitaḥ diṣṭyā na vimatiṃ kāṃ cid bhajitvā tu parājitaḥ
english: 'By good fortune I never turned back from enmity to be vanquished like a common man; by good fortune I was overthrown without ever stooping to any baseness.'

sanskrit: suptaṃ vātha pramattaṃ vā yathā hanyād viṣeṇa vā evaṃ vyutkrāntadharmeṇa vyutkramya samayaṃ hataḥ
english: 'As one might slay a man asleep, or off his guard, or by poison — even so, by one who had cast off righteousness, was I slain through the breaking of the compact.'

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā mahābhāgaḥ kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ kṛpaḥ śāradvataś caiva vaktavyā vacanān mama
english: 'The greatly blessed Aśvatthāman, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvata clan, and Kṛpa, son of Śaradvat — these are to be told in my words:'

sanskrit: adharmeṇa pravṛttānāṃ pāṇḍavānām anekaśaḥ viśvāsaṃ samayaghnānāṃ na yūyaṃ gantum arhatha
english: 'In the Pāṇḍavas, who have so many times acted by unrighteousness and broken their compacts, you must place no trust.'

sanskrit: vātikāṃś cābravīd rājā putras te satyavikramaḥ adharmād bhīmasenena nihato 'haṃ yathā raṇe
english: And the king, your son of truthful valor, spoke also to the messengers: 'Tell them how I was slain in battle by Bhīmasena through unrighteousness.'

sanskrit: so 'haṃ droṇaṃ svargagataṃ śalyakarṇāv ubhau tathā vṛṣasenaṃ mahāvīryaṃ śakuniṃ cāpi saubalam
english: 'I shall follow after Droṇa, gone to heaven, and both Śalya and Karṇa likewise, and the mighty Vṛṣasena, and Śakuni too, the son of Subala,'

sanskrit: jalasaṃdhaṃ mahāvīryaṃ bhagadattaṃ ca pārthivam saumadattiṃ maheṣvāsaṃ saindhavaṃ ca jayadratham
english: 'Jalasaṃdha of great valor, and king Bhagadatta, the son of Somadatta, mighty archer, and Jayadratha the lord of the Sindhus,'

sanskrit: duḥśāsanapurogāṃś ca bhrātṝn ātmasamāṃs tathā dauḥśāsaniṃ ca vikrāntaṃ lakṣmaṇaṃ cātmajāv ubhau
english: 'and my brothers, with Duḥśāsana at their head, equal to my very self, and the valiant son of Duḥśāsana, and Lakṣmaṇa — my own two sons —'

sanskrit: etāṃś cānyāṃś ca subahūn madīyāṃś ca sahasraśaḥ pṛṣṭhato 'nugamiṣyāmi sārthahīna ivādhvagaḥ
english: 'these and very many others of mine by the thousand I shall follow from behind, like a traveler bereft of his caravan.'

sanskrit: kathaṃ bhrātṝn hatāñ śrutvā bhartāraṃ ca svasā mama rorūyamāṇā duḥkhārtā duḥśalā sā bhaviṣyati
english: 'How, on hearing of her slain brothers and her slain husband, will my sister Duḥśalā fare, wailing aloud, stricken with grief?'

sanskrit: snuṣābhiḥ prasnuṣābhiś ca vṛddho rājā pitā mama gāndhārīsahitaḥ krośan kāṃ gatiṃ pratipatsyate
english: 'And my aged father the king, together with Gāndhārī, with his daughters-in-law and their daughters-in-law, lamenting — what refuge shall he find?'

sanskrit: nūnaṃ lakṣmaṇamātāpi hataputrā hateśvarā vināśaṃ yāsyati kṣipraṃ kalyāṇī pṛthulocanā
english: 'Surely Lakṣmaṇa's mother too, her son slain and her lord slain, the gracious, large-eyed lady, will swiftly go to her destruction.'

sanskrit: yadi jānāti cārvākaḥ parivrāḍ vāgviśāradaḥ kariṣyati mahābhāgo dhruvaṃ so 'pacitiṃ mama
english: 'If Cārvāka the wandering ascetic, that master of speech, comes to know of this, the greatly blessed one will surely exact requital for me.'

sanskrit: samantapañcake puṇye triṣu lokeṣu viśrute ahaṃ nidhanam āsādya lokān prāpsyāmi śāśvatān
english: 'At holy Samantapañcaka, renowned throughout the three worlds, having met my death, I shall attain the everlasting worlds.'

sanskrit: tato janasahasrāṇi bāṣpapūrṇāni māriṣa pralāpaṃ nṛpateḥ śrutvā vidravanti diśo daśa
english: Then thousands of people, their eyes brimming with tears, O honored one, hearing the lament of the king, fled away in all ten directions.

sanskrit: sasāgaravanā ghorā pṛthivī sacarācarā cacālātha sanirhrādā diśaś caivāvilābhavan
english: The dread earth, with its seas and forests, with all that moves and is unmoving, then trembled with a roar, and the quarters of the sky grew turbid.

sanskrit: te droṇaputram āsādya yathāvṛttaṃ nyavedayan vyavahāraṃ gadāyuddhe pārthivasya ca ghātanam
english: They, coming to the son of Droṇa, reported all as it had befallen — the manner of the mace-duel and the slaying of the king.

sanskrit: tad ākhyāya tataḥ sarve droṇaputrasya bhārata dhyātvā ca suciraṃ kālaṃ jagmur ārtā yathāgatam
english: Having related this to the son of Droṇa, O Bhārata, they all, brooding for a long while, departed grief-stricken by the way they had come.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca vātikānāṃ sakāśāt tu śrutvā duryodhanaṃ hatam hataśiṣṭās tato rājan kauravāṇāṃ mahārathāḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: Having heard from the messengers that Duryodhana was slain, the great chariot-warriors of the Kauravas who survived the slaughter, O king —

sanskrit: vinirbhinnāḥ śitair bāṇair gadātomaraśaktibhiḥ aśvatthāmā kṛpaś caiva kṛtavarmā ca sātvataḥ tvaritā javanair aśvair āyodhanam upāgaman
english: pierced through by sharp arrows, by maces, javelins, and spears — Aśvatthāman, and Kṛpa, and Kṛtavarman of the Sātvatas — came in haste upon swift horses to the field of battle.

sanskrit: tatrāpaśyan mahātmānaṃ dhārtarāṣṭraṃ nipātitam prabhagnaṃ vāyuvegena mahāśālaṃ yathā vane
english: There they beheld the great-souled son of Dhṛtarāṣṭra struck down, broken as a mighty sāla tree in the forest is broken by the force of the wind.

sanskrit: bhūmau viveṣṭamānaṃ taṃ rudhireṇa samukṣitam mahāgajam ivāraṇye vyādhena vinipātitam
english: writhing upon the ground, drenched with blood, like a great elephant in the wild brought down by a hunter,

sanskrit: vivartamānaṃ bahuśo rudhiraughapariplutam yadṛcchayā nipatitaṃ cakram ādityagocaram
english: rolling about again and again, awash in a flood of blood, fallen as if by chance — like the disk of the sun cast down from the sky,

sanskrit: mahāvātasamutthena saṃśuṣkam iva sāgaram pūrṇacandram iva vyomni tuṣārāvṛtamaṇḍalam
english: like an ocean dried up by a mighty gale, like the full moon in the heavens with its orb veiled in mist,

sanskrit: reṇudhvastaṃ dīrghabhujaṃ mātaṅgasamavikramam vṛtaṃ bhūtagaṇair ghoraiḥ kravyādaiś ca samantataḥ yathā dhanaṃ lipsamānair bhṛtyair nṛpatisattamam
english: begrimed with dust, long-armed, of prowess equal to an elephant's, that best of kings encircled on every side by dreadful hosts of spirits and flesh-eating beasts, as though by servants greedy to seize his wealth,

sanskrit: bhrukuṭīkṛtavaktrāntaṃ krodhād udvṛttacakṣuṣam sāmarṣaṃ taṃ naravyāghraṃ vyāghraṃ nipatitaṃ yathā
english: his brows knit at the corners of his face, his eyes rolled upward in wrath — that tiger among men still full of fury, like a tiger struck down.
